lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna de Fátima | Lesson 10 -- I'd Like That
lesson.grammar_point: would like (I would like / Would you like?) for wants and polite requests

listenings.text: Good afternoon. This is the restaurant on the corner. Your table for six is ready at twelve thirty. Today the plate of the day is fish with rice, and there is a vegetarian option too. Would you like coffee after lunch? Please tell us when you arrive. See you soon.

In my country we do not wait for the bill. We go to the counter and we pay there. Here it is different: you sit, you wait, and the waiter brings the bill to the table. In my first week I always stood up too early. Now I know what to do. I say: can I have the bill, please? And I wait.

extra_audio.text: Giovanna arrives at the restaurant with the London team. The waiter shows them the table. She reads the menu in English. She orders fish and a coffee. At the end she asks for the bill.

paras: The restaurant is next to the office, on the corner. It is small, and it is always full at one o'clock. We have a table for six at twelve thirty.
The menu is in Portuguese and in English. There is a plate of the day, and it changes every day.
Daniel does not eat meat, so he would like the fish or the vegetables. The other two would like a coffee after lunch.
The bill comes to the table at the end. The company pays, so nobody has to wait at the counter.
